dispatch: DA 280; REV 203's diagnosis, executed not read
THE_DEFECT: MY LEDGER PRINTED 6/6 FOR THE WRONG REASON. The status branch ended in `else: status = "SATISFIED"`, so any row that matched no earlier branch READ AS SATISFIED AND COUNTED. A probe that crashed produced `probed: false`, which matched nothing, and fell through to that default.

EXECUTED_NOT_READ.the_probe_dies: PROBE_GATE_6 built ReplayInputs without the now-required `action_keys_sha256` -> TypeError: ReplayInputs.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument
EXECUTED_NOT_READ.and_it_dies_outside_its_own_run_guard: so nothing is printed at all
EXECUTED_NOT_READ.the_harness_indexes_empty_output: IndexError: list index out of range, from r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1]
EXECUTED_NOT_READ.the_row_records: {'probed': False, 'reason': 'IndexError: list index out of range'}
EXECUTED_NOT_READ.measured_live_before_the_fix: gates_satisfied 6/6 with THREE rows probed=false -- gates 1, 2 and 6 -- and no_labelled_score_permitted FALSE on the strength of it

REVS_SHARPEST_POINT_AND_IT_IS_CORRECT: the same branch would have printed 6/6 the round before, when gate 6 GENUINELY failed. A ledger with a default-satisfied branch is not a second instrument, it is an echo. Verified here by driving `row_status` directly with a crashed-probe input.

THE_FIX.1_the_probe_runs: every ReplayInputs in PROBE_GATE_6 is built through one helper that supplies `action_keys_sha256`
THE_FIX.2_unprobed_is_its_own_status: PROPERTIES_NOT_PROBED. SATISFIED is now reachable ONLY through an explicit `props['probed'] is True`; there is no default branch left
THE_FIX.3_the_predicate: gates_satisfied counts only rows with probed: true -- stated in `row_status` AND again at the counting site, so an edit to either cannot quietly restore the default
THE_FIX.4_every_gate_is_probed: the NO_DA_PROBE exemption is GONE. An exemption and a crash were indistinguishable in the output: both produced probed: false. Probes were written for gates 1 and 2, so `probed` means the same thing on every row
THE_FIX.5_negative_control: row_status(present, DRIVEN_GREEN, {'probed': False, 'reason': 'IndexError...'}) == PROPERTIES_NOT_PROBED -- REV's exact case, reproduced as a cell, plus a cell proving a truthy non-True (1) cannot pass

GATE_1s_PROBE_IS_SAME_SEAT_AND_SAYS_SO: DA wrote both the module and its probe. It establishes COVERAGE of §5 item 1's stated properties; it is not a second instrument, and agreement between it and gate 1's own cells is not convergence (rule 38). Carried on the row as `same_seat_probe`.
A_FIXTURE_ERROR_FOUND_WHILE_FIXING_THIS: my new gate-2 probe asserted that a post-decision row is REFUSED as FUTURE_KNOWLEDGE_IN_SOURCE. It is not: be_sigma_30m EXCLUDES such rows and COUNTS them in `n_rows_after_decision`, which is what §5 actually requires -- no future knowledge in the estimate. The refusal is a structural backstop on an already-filtered series. I wrote the property from my expectation of the MECHANISM rather than from the plan's REQUIREMENT, and it failed against correct code. Fourth fixture error of this shape this session.

DE_REVIEW_205_FINDING_CREDITED_AND_FIXED.the_finding: `_root()` ran `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` with NO directory, so it was CWD-DEPENDENT, and returned '.' on failure. Driven from /tmp the repo could not be resolved, every count came back 0, and the landed-path control fired
DE_REVIEW_205_FINDING_CREDITED_AND_FIXED.why_it_matters_here: 0 landed paths is exactly the input that made rows read UNKNOWN or, before this dispatch, default-SATISFIED
DE_REVIEW_205_FINDING_CREDITED_AND_FIXED.the_fix: resolve from THIS MODULE's own location first, then the cwd, and REFUSE NO_REPOSITORY_RESOLVABLE if neither is a repository. A path this file cannot verify is not one it may guess at
DE_REVIEW_205_FINDING_CREDITED_AND_FIXED.verified: DE's exact command re-run from /tmp with a minimal environment: the landed-path control now PASSES with counts 1 and 1
DE_REVIEW_205_FINDING_CREDITED_AND_FIXED.one_correction_to_the_report: DE reported 'exit code 0 in BOTH cases'. Measured: in the broken state the falsifier exited 1 with real FAIL cells; after the fix it exits 0 with none. The apparent FAIL lines in the fixed run are a grep artifact -- two PASS labels contain the literal text '[PASS]/[FAIL] lines', the name of the cell-counting method, so `grep -c '[FAIL]'` matches them. I reproduced that false positive myself before spotting it

THE_TWO_EXECUTING_REFS.why_recorded: REV reported the refs diverged by one BE commit each -- chain 1764deb, runner d559c88, same title, two shas -- while all lane modules were byte-identical. Recorded so a reader meeting two shas is not surprised
THE_TWO_EXECUTING_REFS.the_rule: a gate is satisfied by the BLOB on both refs, not by the heads matching. Two shas with identical modules is a normal state and blocks nothing. Computed every run, never assumed

AND_THIS_6_OF_6_IS_NOT_THE_EARLIER_ONE: the earlier 6/6 counted three rows that were never probed. This one counts six rows that each drove their module's falsifier from the ref's bytes AND passed a DA property probe against the same bytes. The number is the same; what stands behind it is not.
STEP_6_FREEZE_STILL_BLOCKED_BY_ITS_OWN_G: DA 278's draft remains UNLANDED and carries 15 blocking gaps of its own -- P&L and the immutable-input manifest have no implementation, and the quote mapping satisfies 1 of §7's 8 clauses. Six of six on the BUILD gates does not close those.
